AI chip (GPU / TPU) shipments are limited by several factors. But estimating shipment volume from just infrastructure power supply and max chip power (TDP) oversimplifies things and ignores how it actually works in practice. Here's why: 1. Chips don't run at max power all the time. 2. Same power, newer chips produce more tokens. That drives demand for new chips. 3. Same power, more chips running in parallel at lower load will often produce more tokens than fewer chips at high or full load.
AI 晶片（GPU / TPU）的出貨受數種因素限制，但是如果只用「基礎建設的電力供應」和「晶片最大功耗（TDP）」這兩個因素來判斷出貨量，不但過度簡化，也忽略了實務上的運作方式，原因如下： 1. 晶片不會一直以最大功耗運轉。 2. 相同供電下，新一代晶片能產出更多 token，帶動新晶片需求。 3. 相同供電下，多顆晶片降載並行，在許多情境下比少顆高負載（或滿載）產出更多 token。

Elon Musk quickly impressed Franz von Holzhausen, persuading him to join Tesla and leave behind a successful career at Mazda. Franz recalls: "For somebody who's going to put rockets into space, car is actually not that hard, and his vision for the car and his sustainable direction and message is exactly what I'm looking for." In the summer of 2008, Franz already had the kind of automotive career most designers dream about, having penned sports cars at GM and led design at Mazda North America, while Tesla was near bankruptcy. But after meeting Elon Musk at SpaceX and going for a drive together in an early Roadster while people on the street stopped to stare, Franz walked away from his secure job to start designing the Model S from a blank sheet of paper. When he later explained why he took that leap of faith into a startup with no guarantees, his answer came down to Elon's total commitment: "Tesla was all in."

$HPE CEO: "We expect supply of memory, NAND, and many other critical components to remain constrained to at least H2 2028." $DELL Vice Chairman: "there’s nothing that suggests that we're going to see price declines in enterprise NAND and DRAM for servers." JP Morgan note: - Per OpenRouter, overall token spend continued to increase (+8% M/M growth), while volume pricing declined -39% M/M. - A100 GPU prices increased, H100 and B200 prices also continued to increase M/M - DRAM price gains moderated, while NAND spot declined. On the latter part, I covered China selling inventory on NAND/eSSD spot markets. This was procurement delays around $NVDA GPUs/DRAM shortages, demand to re-accelerate after component arrive. (source Phison CEO) Enterprise NAND pricing might see different rates than spot markets, as seen with Dell Chairman comments. TLDR: - Token spend continues to grow despite users shifting to cheaper Chinese models - Bullish comments on DRAM duration (also seen with $AMBA earnings), but consumer demand weakening - Compute pricing continues to increase in November - More nuanced for NAND, weakness in near term NAND spot markets (with expected rebound after GPUs/DRAM/components arrive), enterprise NAND markets seem resilient.

@NaveenGRao sold Nervana to Intel and MosaicML to Databricks. His third company, @unconvai, is building something that looks nothing like a GPU. His argument: AI is now limited by energy, so the number that matters is joules per token. Getting there means dropping the von Neumann split between memory and compute and building a machine that is "programmed by weights." To learn fast, they tape out a new chip roughly every three months. Their first test chip, a system of coupled oscillators, generated small images at about 900 nanojoules each, against about 50 millijoules on a GPU. @dylan522p asks why so many analog chips blew their lead once you count the conversion costs, whether programmability still matters when NVIDIA is king, and whether we will stop buying computers and start buying intelligence tokens. SpaceX has agreed to forgo $738 million in U.S. federal broadband subsidies and instead provide free @Starlink hardware to eligible American households. NTIA: "To ensure that no consumer at a Covered BSL is left behind, the provider (SpaceX) will serve the covered BSLs as this agreement provides. This includes providing customer premises equipment at no cost to new subscribers, so that households at covered BSL do not face the upfront equipment costs. Additionally, the provider’s broadband service will be subject to the same delivery timelines and performance testing requirements applicable to all recipients of BEAD funds." Under the new agreement, SpaceX would: • Provide free Starlink hardware to eligible households. • Guarantee minimum download speeds of 100 Mbps and upload speeds of 20 Mbps. • Offer a low-cost monthly internet plan. • Commit to providing service for 10 years. • Continue to comply with federal performance testing requirements. The agreement will save American taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars while accelerating high-speed internet access in underserved rural communities. In exchange, SpaceX would be exempt from most BEAD-related financial audits, procurement requirements and administrative reporting, while remaining subject to network performance testing.
